**Economic Factors of Social Change**

Economic transformations drive social change through several mechanisms. Industrialization shifts labor patterns, urbanizing populations and altering family structures. Income inequality creates class consciousness and mobilizes political movements. Technological disruption displaces workers, forcing educational and occupational adaptation.

Trade integration exposes societies to foreign ideas and consumption patterns, reshaping cultural values. Inflation and recession trigger social instability; prosperity enables progressive reforms. Resource scarcity sparks competition and conflict, while abundance permits social experimentation.

Labor market changes—wage stagnation, precarious work, skill premiums—reshape generational attitudes toward institutions and authority. Economic mobility (or immobility) determines whether social hierarchies persist or dissolve.

Wealth concentration either consolidates power or generates redistributive pressure. Consumer capitalism shapes identity and aspiration. Ultimately, economic capacity determines which social changes societies can afford and which demands they must address.
